statement: For a weakly reversible finite mass-action network with one linkage class and fixed positive rate constants, if every proper tier sequence of the CTMC has highest stochastic tier contained in highest deterministic tier, then the CTMC is positive recurrent from each specified initial state. The paper's total-rate lower bound on every nonabsorbing class converts the embedded-chain argument to physical-time nonexplosion and positive recurrence; absorbing states are trivial.
interface_and_quantifiers: Complexes C subset N_0^d and finite reaction set R are supplied; propensities are kappa_(y->y') product_i (x_i)_(y_i) 1{x_i>=y_i}, with all kappa strictly positive. The tier premise quantifies over proper sequences in the reachable state space from the initial state. One linkage class and weak reversibility are required.
proof_evidence: Anderson-Cappelletti-Kim, Theorem 6.1 and Lemma 6.5 use a bounded-length favorable reaction word and a fixed-step embedded-chain Foster argument. Theorem 3.1 plus Lemma 3.2 establishes the physical-time conclusion.
cost: The source theorem gives existence, not a quantitative return-time, mixing, stationary-tail, or finite-precision bound. The path probabilities depend on the fixed rates.
strongest_baseline: Complex balance gives an all-order product-form stationary law and nonexplosion on its subclass. Anderson-Kim 2018, Corollary 4.3 is a separate general one-step tier/Foster sufficient condition.
falsifier: A counterexample satisfying the exact single-linkage, weak-reversibility, positive-rate, and all-proper-sequence tier-inclusion hypotheses but failing classwise positive recurrence would contradict the cited theorem.
novelty_boundary: No new recurrence theorem is claimed; this is the external theorem used as the baseline for an internally derived finite recognizer.
unresolved: The premise is sufficient, not necessary, and its failure does not decide recurrence. General higher-dimensional WR recurrence remains UNKNOWN in the sources audited.

statement: For any finite complex set C in N_0^d, the network-wide condition that every lattice proper sequence has stochastic top tier contained in deterministic top tier can be reduced to finitely many exact rational linear-feasibility tests. Acceptance certifies the tier premise of ACK Theorem 6.1 for every reachable class of a supplied one-linkage WR graph on C.
interface_and_quantifiers: The finite integer exponent vectors C are supplied. The checker ranges over every nonempty set I of diverging coordinates and every bounded-coordinate threshold pattern that changes the enabled-source set. This is stronger than checking sequences reachable in one fixed class. Rate constants are not checker inputs beyond the theorem's positivity requirement.
proof_evidence: After subsequence extraction each coordinate is fixed or diverges. Falling factorial propensities have the same log-monomial order as the diverging-coordinate exponents on enabled sources. A bounded projection removes finite log-ratio offsets among tied stochastic-top sources while preserving strict divergent gaps. A failure must have a disabled source strictly above an enabled stochastic-top source: enabled sources have the same stochastic and deterministic ordering. Every strict violation is represented by positive rational weights; rational weights realize a violating sequence by floor(n^w). Each violation is exactly a bounded LP with a common positive margin delta. Threshold values {0} union source exponents produce finitely many strata.
cost: At most sum_(nonempty I subset [d]) (m+1)^(d-|I|) strata and at most m^2 LPs per stratum, with |I|+1 variables and O(m) constraints for m complexes. The delivered code uses exact Fraction vertex enumeration, with combinatorial dimension/constraint cost and potentially large rational intermediates. It has no useful general runtime bound and no complexity/precision analysis beyond this accounting.
strongest_baseline: The cited ACK and Anderson-Kim papers state the stochastic tier criteria and recurrence implications but do not supply this exact all-sequence LP compilation. General exact rational LP algorithms provide a more scalable implementation route but do not remove the proof/reduction obligation.
falsifier: A tier violation not representable by one of the finite strata/LP witnesses, or an LP acceptance despite an explicit lattice sequence with stochastic top outside deterministic top, would refute the reduction or implementation.
novelty_boundary: This run's candidate contribution is the reduction and exact fixture compiler, not the recurrence theorem. Novelty and priority have not been externally checked.
unresolved: The written proof is not machine-verified; the script is a small internal implementation. A failed test returns a tier-condition counterexample candidate, not a recurrence counterexample.

statement: The network A+3D -> A+B+3D -> A+C+3D -> C+3D -> 2B+3D -> A+3D, with rates (1,1,2,1,1), is a four-species, rank-three, deficiency-one, one-linkage WR network of maximum source order five and is not complex balanced. The exact tier checker accepts its all-lattice tier premise. Therefore every nonabsorbing communicating class is positive recurrent, conditional on the internal reduction/code result and the external ACK Theorem 6.1.
interface_and_quantifiers: Finite network and positive rational rates are fixed. The tier checker tests all lattice sequences, hence a stronger premise than the source theorem needs for any individual communicating class.
proof_evidence: The exact checker checks 58 strata and 220 rational LPs and returns accepted=true. Stoichiometric rank and deficiency follow from the five displayed complexes and reaction vectors. Complex-balance equations contradict c_B=1, c_C=1/2, and c_C=c_B^2=1.
cost: Constant-size exact fixture; checker uses Fraction arithmetic. No solver, simulation, or rate-oracle acquisition. The 4th coordinate D=3 contributes a common falling-factorial factor 6 on the displayed class.
strongest_baseline: Complex-balance product form does not cover this rate vector. The classwise conclusion is from ACK Theorem 6.1; this artifact does not improve its coverage.
falsifier: An exact LP counterexample for a missed tier stratum, a checker arithmetic error, a complex-balance solution, or a violation of the one-linkage/WR/rank calculation would falsify the fixture claim.
novelty_boundary: The fixture is an internal stress-test and an instance of a known sufficient theorem; no novelty or priority claim.
unresolved: The checker is not formally verified and exact recurrence is conditional on that check plus the source theorem. No quantitative return time, invariant law, or cross-class tightness follows.

statement: Along the reachable unbounded ray x_n=(n,1,0,3), total-count and entropy one-step generator drifts are positive, but the exact three-step embedded entropy drift is -(29/36) log n + O(1).
interface_and_quantifiers: The fixed fixture above; x_n is reachable since r1,r5,r1 maps x_n to x_(n+1). At x_n only r1 and r2 are enabled, each at rate 6n.
proof_evidence: The exact script enumerates the ten possible endpoints after three jumps and simplifies E[A(X_3)-n] to the rational function in RESULT.txt, with limit -29/36. Since B,C remain bounded and A=n+j with bounded j, V_A(n+j)-V_A(n)=j log n+O(1). The full endpoint expectation, not a single selected word, gives the coefficient.
cost: Exact symbolic arithmetic using SymPy; finite horizon k=3 and ten endpoints. Script output is replayable. No asymptotic numerical fitting.
strongest_baseline: ACK Theorem 6.1 already motivates bounded-step drift when one-step entropy drift fails. This calculation is a higher-order non-complex-balanced fixture for that known mechanism.
falsifier: A symbolic simplification error or a missing enabled transition at any of the ten three-step endpoints would falsify the formula.
novelty_boundary: Internal exact diagnostic only; it does not establish global recurrence, since that conclusion uses the separate all-sequence theorem premise.
unresolved: The ray calculation yields no return-time or stationary-tail bound and is not a general one-step Foster impossibility result.

statement: This cycle neither proves classwise positive recurrence for all higher-order WR networks with at least three species nor produces a genuinely WR transient, null-recurrent, or explosive counterexample.
interface_and_quantifiers: Target: arbitrary finite weakly reversible stochastic mass-action reaction graphs, d>=3, arbitrary fixed positive rate constants, with claims scoped to each communicating class and physical time.
proof_evidence: Nineteen distinct cycle-2 attacks found only exact sufficient subclasses, structured classwise examples, and route-specific escape obstructions. The rank-three non-complex-balanced family is positive recurrent on the explicitly analyzed classes but does not classify all classes or all networks. Closure of the known explosive word adds a faster competing channel, invalidating that candidate route.
cost: No exhaustive search over networks or proof search was completed; negative evidence is scoped to named constructions. Source and agent coverage do not imply nonexistence.
strongest_baseline: All-order complex-balanced product-form/nonexplosion results; rank-one WR recurrence; ACK single-linkage path-tier criterion; and a two-species all-rate claim that remains SOURCE-REPORTED in the available project/conference sources.
falsifier: A complete proof under the stated arbitrary d>=3 interface, or an exactly verified qualifying WR counterexample, would resolve this open status.
novelty_boundary: No field-breaking, novelty, or impossibility claim. The 2D result is marked SOURCE-REPORTED because the checked project page lists the manuscript as in preparation.
unresolved: Find a rate-weighted classwise tier/cycle mechanism that handles nested boundary and tie strata in dimension at least three, or construct a positive-probability nonperiodic escape with summable physical holding times.
